articles.title: Functional outcomes of gluteus medius repair after prior primary THA: a case series with 2-year minimum follow-up.
articles.authors: Quesada-Jimenez R, Rana K, Barda SR, Wallace I, Sugarman EP, Domb BG
articles.population: Patients undergoing open gluteus medius repair after prior total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Modified Harris Hip Score, International Hip Outcome Tool-12, pain scores, patient satisfaction, and complication rates at minimum 2-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Gluteus medius repair after hip replacement led to significant improvements in hip function and pain scores, with high patient satisfaction and low rates of needing further surgery. Most patients achieved meaningful clinical improvements in their symptoms.

articles.title: Assessing the impact of dialysis on short, intermediate, and long-term outcomes following total hip arthroplasty: a propensity-matched analysis.
articles.authors: Gooch BR, Kiritsis NR, Cassidy BP, Ernst BS, Satpathy J, Hartzler M
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement, comparing those requiring dialysis with those not requiring dialysis
articles.outcomes: Adverse events, surgical site infection, infected hip prosthesis, and revision hip replacement at 90 days, 2 years, and 5 years
articles.take_home: Patients on dialysis who have hip replacement surgery experience significantly higher rates of complications including infections and need for repeat surgery at all time points up to 5 years compared to patients not on dialysis. Surgeons should discuss these elevated risks with dialysis patients before recommending elective hip replacement.

articles.title: Pain management in osteoarthritis of the hip using percutaneous obturator nerve neuromodulation with pulsed radiofrequency ablation under CT guidance.
articles.authors: Kosmoliaptsis P, Makri D, Michailidis A, Dimou G, Mingou G, Papadimitriou I, et al.
articles.population: Patients with hip osteoarthritis refractory to conservative treatment
articles.sample_size: 33 hips in 30 patients, mean age 69 years
articles.outcomes: Pain intensity measured on visual analogue scale at 1 week, 1, 3, 6 and 12 months post-procedure; complication rates
articles.take_home: Percutaneous radiofrequency ablation of the obturator nerve significantly reduced hip pain with no reported complications, and pain relief lasted up to 12 months in patients with mild-to-moderate osteoarthritis. However, in patients with severe osteoarthritis, pain relief was short-lived and pain returned after about 3 months.

articles.title: Current concepts in isolated and combined injuries of the medial collateral ligament complex, part II: The anteromedial knee instability classification.
articles.authors: Runer A, Bouguennec N, Wierer G, Robinson J, Amis A, Herbst E, et al.
articles.study_type: Review article presenting a classification system
articles.population: Patients with medial collateral ligament injuries, isolated or combined with anterior cruciate ligament injuries
articles.outcomes: Anteromedial knee instability classification graded as A, B or C based on valgus stress testing and external rotation testing
articles.take_home: A new classification system helps doctors assess the severity of medial knee ligament injuries by examining how loose the knee is, which can guide treatment decisions for both isolated ligament injuries and combined injuries involving multiple ligaments.

articles.title: Feasibility of repeat tibial tubercle osteotomy in re-revision knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Walkay S, Koppolu S, Sharma A, Jonas S, Agarwal S
articles.population: Patients undergoing re-revision knee arthroplasty with repeat tibial tubercle osteotomy
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union, nonunion, proximal migration, crest fragmentation, extensor lag, range of motion and soft tissue complications
articles.take_home: Sequential repeat tibial tubercle osteotomy during re-revision knee replacement surgery heals successfully in 97.6% of cases with low complication rates. Only 2 cases of nonunion occurred and there were no soft tissue complications or extension problems.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of femoral bone tunnel fixation and onlay fixation techniques for medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction: a systematic review.
articles.authors: Nam HH, Velasquez-Hammerle MV, Merkely G, Leite CBG, Nakanishi Y, Nagai K, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of femoral fixation techniques for medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.population: Adults with recurrent patellofemoral instability undergoing isolated medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.sample_size: 4100 patients across 80 studies (3851 in bone tunnel group, 249 in onlay fixation group)
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction measured by Kujala score and recurrent dislocation rates. Bone tunnel group mean Kujala score 87.9, onlay group 91.4. Redislocation rates 2.0% for bone tunnel and 1.7% for onlay fixation
articles.take_home: Both bone tunnel and onlay fixation methods for this type of knee ligament surgery produce good results with low rates of the knee dislocating again. Onlay fixation, though used less often, appears to work just as well as bone tunnel methods and may be a useful alternative when bone tunnels are not possible.

articles.title: The Current Landscape of Fragility Fracture Care in the People's Republic of China.
articles.authors: Wong RMY, Yang M, Zhao C, Liu C, Cheng KYK, Cheung WH, et al.
articles.population: Patients with fragility fractures in China
articles.outcomes: Current treatment approaches including robotic systems, total hip arthroplasty, multidisciplinary care, and prevalence of sarcopenia
articles.take_home: Fragility fracture care in China is evolving to include robotic technology and newer surgical approaches, with growing recognition that managing these fractures requires multidisciplinary teams and addressing muscle weakness, which is common in affected patients.

articles.title: Early Surgical Management of Periprosthetic Hip Fracture Does Not Reduce Mortality or Cardiopulmonary Complications: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.authors: Papalia AG, Ricotti RG, Frappa N, Alben MG, Ozdag Y, Sutton R
articles.study_type: Propensity-matched observational study using national database
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing revision hip replacement surgery for fractures around existing hip implants
articles.outcomes: Primary: mortality at 30 days, 90 days and 1 year. Secondary: heart attacks, blood clots, lung clots, pneumonia, kidney injury, sepsis, infection, wound problems and need for blood transfusion
articles.take_home: Having surgery within two days of diagnosis did not reduce death or serious heart and lung complications compared with surgery after two days. Early surgery was linked to needing more blood transfusions, but this difference may not be clinically important and should not rush surgical decisions.

articles.title: The Aggregation of Marginal Gains in Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Practical Framework for Scalable, High-Quality Care.
articles.authors: Jenkins S, Smitterberg CW, Scuderi GR, Mont MA
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip and knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Operating room efficiency, wound management, blood management, discharge planning, follow-up care, workforce sustainability, and patient access
articles.take_home: Small improvements made systematically across different stages of joint replacement surgery (before, during and after) can add up to meaningful gains in hospital capacity and efficiency. The study outlines a framework for testing and keeping only those changes that actually improve care without compromising safety or patient experience.

articles.title: Mid- to long-term follow-up of trabecular titanium acetabular cups in hip revision surgery for acetabular bone defects.
articles.authors: Siracusano L, Meo F, Bruschetta A, Cacciola G, Alibrandi A, Leonetti D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing hip revision surgery for severe acetabular bone defects (Paprosky grade IIa or higher)
articles.outcomes: Oxford Hip Score, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index, Oxford Hip Score for pain and function, Work-related Quality of Life, radiographic integration, complications and revisions, implant survival
articles.take_home: Trabecular titanium cups provided good pain relief and function in patients with severe hip socket bone loss, with 96.3% of implants surviving at 12 years. Complications occurred in 9.2% of patients, most commonly hip dislocation.

articles.title: When do patients resume driving after fast-track hip and knee arthroplasty: a cohort study of 408 patients.
articles.authors: Danielsen O, Lauritsen J, Lindberg-Larsen M
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty, total knee arthroplasty, or medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty in a fast-track setup
articles.outcomes: Timing of driving resumption after surgery; influence of patient and surgical factors on resumption timing
articles.take_home: Most patients resumed driving within 6 weeks of surgery, with those having knee resurfacing (mUKA) and left leg surgery returning to driving sooner (around 4 weeks). Women were three times more likely to take longer than 6 weeks to resume driving.

articles.title: A comparison of revision risk between lateral knee replacement and total knee replacement: results from the Dutch Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Koenraadt-van Oost I, Van Boekel LC, Hoorntje A, Kerkhoffs GMMJ, Mulder PGH, Van Steenbergen LN, et al.
articles.study_type: Comparative observational study using registry data
articles.population: Patients undergoing lateral knee replacement or total knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 847 lateral knee replacements and 240,047 total knee replacements (total cohort); 560 lateral and 155,621 total knee replacements (subgroup with complete data)
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery rates; Kaplan-Meier survival analysis; revision hazard ratios
articles.take_home: Lateral knee replacements had a significantly higher risk of needing revision surgery compared to total knee replacements, with roughly double the revision risk in the overall analysis. This finding suggests lateral knee replacements may be less durable than total knee replacements, though lateral knee replacements are rarely performed.

articles.title: Modified 6-Factor Frailty Index Enhances Risk Stratification in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Swaminathan N, Welsh C, Wagner P, Panwalker N, Richards A, Areti A, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 30-day adverse outcomes including reoperation, readmission, mortality, and wound complications
articles.take_home: Adding a blood albumin measurement to an existing frailty scoring system improved the ability to predict who would have complications after revision hip surgery. Patients with low albumin levels had significantly higher risks of adverse outcomes, suggesting that checking albumin levels before surgery could help identify higher-risk patients.

articles.title: Low graft re-rupture rate after primary ACL reconstruction using a modified MacIntosh iliotibial band technique with gracilis augmentation: Minimum 6-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Bouyge B, Gerometta A, Valentin E, Moussa M, Lepidas N, Khiami F, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary ACL reconstruction using modified MacIntosh iliotibial band technique with gracilis augmentation
articles.outcomes: Graft re-rupture rate, functional scores (IKDC and Lysholm), return-to-sport rate, complications
articles.take_home: This surgical technique resulted in a low graft re-rupture rate of 4.9% at 6+ years follow-up, with 91.6% of patients returning to sport and good functional scores. Younger patients and those with meniscal tears were at higher risk of graft failure.

articles.title: Inducible displacement measured with radiostereometric analysis in primary knee arthroplasty: a systematic review of clinical studies.
articles.authors: Jurgens-Lahnstein JH, Teilmann JF, Petersen ET, Rytter S, Stilling M, Laende E
articles.population: Patients who had primary knee replacement surgery
articles.outcomes: Inducible displacement of knee implants measured using radiostereometric analysis, particularly maximum total point motion during weightbearing
articles.take_home: Radiostereometric analysis can measure how much knee replacement implants move when weight is put on them, and this might help identify implants at risk of failure. However, current research does not yet provide a clear threshold value that doctors can use to reliably spot which implants will need revision surgery.

articles.title: Hip arthroscopy in Sweden: a nationwide registry study of socioeconomic characteristics, regional variation, and sick leave patterns.
articles.authors: Wadstrom MG, Stalman A, Worner T, Eek F, Hailer NP, Kraus-Schmitz J, et al.
articles.population: People aged 18-65 years in Sweden who underwent hip arthroscopy between 2006 and 2018, compared with age and sex-matched reference population
articles.sample_size: 4,633 individuals undergoing hip arthroscopy and 23,060 matched reference individuals
articles.outcomes: Demographic and socioeconomic characteristics including education, employment, income, sick leave patterns, and regional variation in hip arthroscopy incidence
articles.take_home: People who had hip arthroscopy in Sweden were more likely to be employed and earn higher incomes than the general population. They also took more sick leave both before and after surgery, and the likelihood of having the procedure varied significantly depending on which region they lived in.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Measures Collection Method by Timeframe: Different Strategies for Different Times.
articles.authors: Ren BO, Zhu Q, Kim Mhsa T, Hallstrom BR, Dailey EA
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total joint arthroplasty (hip or knee)
articles.sample_size: 18,602 patients with complete surveys out of 71,672 cases
articles.outcomes: Response rates and collection methods for patient-reported outcome measures at preoperative, early postoperative, and one-year timepoints
articles.take_home: Different collection methods work best at different times after joint replacement surgery - in-person collection works better before and shortly after surgery, whilst email links become more effective at one year. Only about 29% of patients completed all required surveys according to standards, suggesting collection strategies need to be adapted to each patient and timeframe.

articles.title: Preoperative Pain Sensitivity Has a Greater Impact on Clinical Outcomes Than Coronal Alignment Strategy in Robotic-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kawaguchi K, Tay ML, Farrington WJ, van Rooyen R, Bayan A, Young SW
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Forgotten Joint Score and Oxford Knee Score at two years; relationship between preoperative pain sensitivity and patient-reported outcomes
articles.take_home: Patients' preoperative pain sensitivity was a stronger predictor of knee surgery satisfaction than the surgical alignment technique used. In patients with low pain sensitivity, a functional alignment approach gave better results than mechanical alignment, but this difference disappeared in patients with high pain sensitivity.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and complication rates following medial collateral ligament reconstruction using Achilles tendon allograft or hamstring tendon autograft: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Sian R, See A, Alqeisi T, Meena A, Dalgleish S, de Sa D, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 16 years and over undergoing medial collateral ligament reconstruction with Achilles tendon allograft or hamstring tendon autograft
articles.sample_size: 16 studies: 107 patients with Achilles tendon allograft and 275 patients with hamstring autograft
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (IKDC and Lysholm scores), graft failure rates, and complication rates including infections, instability and hardware issues
articles.take_home: Both Achilles tendon allograft and hamstring tendon autograft significantly improved patient outcomes after medial collateral ligament reconstruction, with similar functional scores. Achilles tendon allograft had a higher complication rate (11.2% versus 4.0%), but the available evidence is not strong enough to confirm that one graft type is definitively better than the other.

articles.title: Intraprosthetic dislocation in modular dual-mobility: does the company matter? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Shanaa J, Stoebner J, Di Pauli von Treuheim T, Schwarzkopf R, Cohen-Rosenblum A, Aggarwal VK
articles.population: Patients receiving modular dual-mobility hip implants
articles.outcomes: Intraprosthetic dislocation incidence and reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Intraprosthetic dislocation in modular dual-mobility hip implants is rare, occurring in fewer than 1 in 250 cases overall. The study found no significant differences in safety between different manufacturers, though there were very few non-Stryker implants reported.

articles.title: Upward versus downward pelvic obliquity in dysplastic hip osteoarthritis: direction-specific factors associated with residual obliquity after total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Yokoi H, Osawa Y, Funahashi H, Ozawa Y, Takegami Y, Imagama S
articles.population: Patients with dysplastic hip osteoarthritis undergoing total hip arthroplasty with pelvic obliquity of 2 degrees or more
articles.sample_size: 116 patients (21 men, 95 women); 35 with upward pelvic obliquity, 81 with downward pelvic obliquity
articles.outcomes: Factors associated with residual pelvic obliquity after surgery, including leg lengthening, lumbar scoliosis angle, and lumbar lateral bending mobility
articles.take_home: The direction of pelvic tilt before hip replacement surgery predicts whether it will persist afterwards. Greater lengthening of the leg during surgery was linked to upward tilt persistence, whilst spine curvature and reduced spinal flexibility were linked to downward tilt persistence.

articles.title: Prevention of Periprosthetic Fractures: What Should We Be Doing to Address This Impending Epidemic?
articles.authors: Lamb JN, Whitehouse M
articles.population: Patients with total hip arthroplasties
articles.outcomes: Incidence and consequences of periprosthetic fractures including mortality, reoperation rates and implant survival
articles.take_home: Periprosthetic fractures after hip replacement are becoming more common and carry serious risks including death and need for further surgery. Surgeons should take a joined-up approach involving multiple specialties to help prevent these fractures.

articles.title: Development of osteoarthritis in adults with untreated hip dysplasia: a longitudinal observational study.
articles.authors: Vinge R, Rogmark C, Wenger D, Overgaard S, Tiderius CJ
articles.population: Adults aged 20-70 years with unilateral hip dysplasia, no osteoarthritis at baseline
articles.outcomes: Osteoarthritis incidence, time to osteoarthritis development, and minimum joint space width at follow-up
articles.take_home: Over a median follow-up of 12.5 years, osteoarthritis developed in similar proportions of dysplastic and non-dysplastic hips, with no meaningful differences in timing or severity of joint space narrowing between the two groups.

articles.title: Preoperative Medial Proximal Tibial Angle Does Not Influence Clinical Outcomes Following Mobile-Bearing Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kinoshita T, Bunyoz KI, Mortensen KRL, Jensen CB, Gromov K, Troelsen A
articles.population: Patients with antero-medial knee osteoarthritis undergoing mobile-bearing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Score at three months, one year, and two years post-operatively; postoperative tibial component alignment
articles.take_home: The angle of the tibia bone before surgery did not affect how well patients did after unicompartmental knee replacement over two years. Patients improved similarly regardless of their initial bone angle.

articles.title: The Safety of Postoperative Selective Cyclooxygenase-2 Inhibitors in Chronically Anticoagulated Patients Undergoing Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tummala S, Valencia A, Chen AF, Bounajem G, Sambandam SN
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database with propensity-score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip replacement on chronic anticoagulation between 2015 and 2025
articles.outcomes: Primary outcomes: blood transfusion and readmission at 30, 90, and 180 days. Secondary outcomes: reoperation, hip dislocation, blood clots, pulmonary embolism, kidney injury, emergency department visits, and opioid use
articles.take_home: Patients taking COX-2 inhibitor painkillers (celecoxib or meloxicam) after hip replacement whilst on anticoagulation did not have higher bleeding or readmission rates compared to those who did not take them, and they used fewer opioid painkillers. The study suggests these medications can be used safely in this group, though further prospective research is needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Assessment of Acetabular Component Anteversion Following Total Hip Arthroplasty: Current Imaging Techniques and Limitations.
articles.authors: Edelstein A, Smitterberg CW, Amanatullah DF, Chen AF, Mont MA
articles.population: Patients who have undergone total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Accuracy, precision, repeatability and limitations of radiographic and CT-based techniques for measuring acetabular component anteversion and inclination
articles.take_home: X-rays are the most readily available way to check hip replacement positioning, but CT scans of the whole pelvis provide more reliable measurements, especially when there are concerns about hip instability or component failure. Doctors need to understand the strengths and weaknesses of each imaging method when assessing problematic hip replacements.

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Treatment Strategies for Fungal Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Rattanaprichavej P, Laoruengthana A, Chinwatanawongwan B, Towiwat P, Jarusriwanna A, Boonpattharatthiti K, et al.
articles.population: Patients with fungal periprosthetic joint infection (infection around hip or knee replacements)
articles.outcomes: Treatment success rates comparing different surgical approaches including debridement with antibiotic and implant retention (DAIR), one-stage revision, two-stage revision, three-stage revision, implant resection, arthrodesis, amputation, and antifungal suppression
articles.take_home: Most surgical approaches for fungal joint replacement infections had similar success rates, but debridement with antibiotic and implant retention (DAIR) was significantly less successful and should be avoided. The choice between other surgical options may depend on individual patient factors.

articles.title: Low Back Pain and Depression Are Associated with Worse Patient-Reported Outcomes After Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Haji Boloori F, Kubiak A, Rezazadeh Shirazi A, Nelson B, Ciolacu I, Meyers M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Six-month change in Oxford Knee Score, achievement of minimum clinically important difference, satisfaction, readmissions and reoperations
articles.take_home: Patients with low back pain and depression before knee replacement had smaller improvements in knee function after surgery, particularly those who improved the least. Having both conditions together had additive rather than combined effects on outcomes.

articles.title: Toward Standardized Reporting in Non-Traumatic Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Recommendations for Clinical Study Design and Reporting.
articles.authors: Cheng EY, Mirzaei A, Sierra RJ, Goodman SB, Hernigou P, Parikh RR, et al.
articles.population: Clinical studies of non-traumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head
articles.outcomes: Proposed standardised reporting framework for ONFH clinical studies, including terminology, diagnostic criteria, staging systems, lesion characterisation, treatment description, and outcome reporting
articles.take_home: Researchers studying osteonecrosis of the hip have used very different methods and reported results differently, making it hard to compare studies and draw clear conclusions. This paper proposes a standard way to report ONFH research to make future studies more comparable and reliable.

articles.title: Association of Recovery and Dissatisfaction with Psychological Distress in Patients Undergoing Total Knee and Hip Arthroplasty in South Australia: A Retrospective Cohort Study of 1,462 Patients.
articles.authors: Aalders MB, Doornberg JN, Benner JL, Jaarsma RL
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee or hip replacement surgery in South Australia
articles.outcomes: Functional recovery, quality of life, and patient satisfaction at one year after surgery, measured against preoperative psychological distress (anxiety and depression)
articles.take_home: Patients with higher levels of anxiety or depression before knee or hip replacement surgery had poorer functional recovery, lower quality of life, and were more likely to be dissatisfied with their surgery one year later. The research suggests that assessing and managing psychological wellbeing before these operations may help improve outcomes.

articles.title: Knee Society Radiographic Evaluation System Update: Standardizing Assessment of Patellar Translation in Resurfaced and Unresurfaced Patellae.
articles.authors: Lonner JH, Mont MA, Scuderi GR, Clarke HD, DellaValle CJ, Haas SB
articles.study_type: Methodological update to radiographic evaluation system
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty with resurfaced or unresurfaced patellae
articles.outcomes: Standardised method for assessing patellar translation on radiographs using appropriate reference points for resurfaced versus unresurfaced patellae
articles.take_home: The Knee Society updated its method for measuring patellar position on X-rays to avoid misinterpreting where the kneecap sits after knee replacement, particularly when surgeons choose not to resurface the natural kneecap.

articles.title: Increased Risk of Periprosthetic Joint Infection Following Aseptic Revision Hip and Knee Arthroplasty With the Use of Non-Cefazolin Alternative Antibiotics.
articles.authors: Panos JA, Mallinger BD, Virk A, Sierra RJ, Abdel MP, Wyles CC
articles.population: Patients undergoing aseptic revision total hip or knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection within follow-up period; association with perioperative antibiotic type, postoperative oral antibiotics, and unexpected positive intraoperative cultures
articles.take_home: Using cefazolin as the perioperative antibiotic during aseptic revision hip or knee surgery significantly reduces the risk of joint infection compared to other antibiotics. Adding oral antibiotics after surgery did not provide extra protection against infection for patients who received cefazolin.

articles.title: Area Deprivation Index, Institutional Practice, and Utilization of Neuraxial Anesthesia in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Garside JC, Joaquin TA, Reeves EE, Shah KS, Crowley BM, Levine BR
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Neuraxial anesthesia utilisation, 90-day emergency department visits, length of stay, 90-day readmissions, complications, and reoperations
articles.take_home: Where patients lived (a measure of deprivation) did not affect whether they received neuraxial anesthesia for knee replacement surgery, but the hospital they attended did. Patients who received neuraxial anesthesia had fewer emergency department visits in the 90 days after surgery compared to those who received general anesthesia.

articles.title: Equivalence of Outcomes Between Ambulatory and Hospital-Based Arthroplasty in Younger and Older Adults.
articles.authors: Pang A, Zamzam M, Hodson N, Pellerito A, North T, Charters M
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective primary total hip or knee arthroplasty, stratified by age (under 75 years and 75 years or older)
articles.outcomes: 90-day readmissions, emergency department visits, reoperations, periprosthetic joint infections, dislocations, periprosthetic fractures, length of stay, procedure duration, and discharge destination
articles.take_home: Total joint replacement at ambulatory surgery centres produced similar safety outcomes to hospital-based surgery within 90 days for both older and younger patients. Age alone should not prevent someone from having their joint replacement at an ambulatory centre, as decisions should be based on individual fitness rather than age cutoffs.

articles.title: There Is No One-Size-Fits-All: Surgical Approach Dictates Optimal Bearing Surface Configuration Choice in 30,000 Total Hip Arthroplasties Over 25 Years.
articles.authors: Cochrane NH, Panos JA, Khela MS, Mabry TM, Perry KI, Pagnano MW, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Dislocation rates at 10 years, stratified by surgical approach (posterior, antero-lateral, direct anterior) and bearing surface configuration (flat/neutral polyethylene, elevated polyethylene, dual-mobility)
articles.take_home: The best bearing surface type for hip replacement depends on which surgical approach is used. Dual-mobility constructs work best with posterior approach surgery, flat polyethylene liners work best with antero-lateral approach, and the direct anterior approach has the lowest dislocation risk regardless of bearing type chosen.

articles.title: Revision Indication Is Associated with Early Mortality After Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Population-Based Study.
articles.authors: Restrepo DJ, Gonzalez-Bravo AE, Guarin Perez SF, Perry KI, Taunton MJ, Abdel MP, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 6,946 patients with 8,667 revision procedures between 1997 and 2023
articles.outcomes: 30-day and 90-day mortality rates and risk factors associated with early death
articles.take_home: Revision hip replacement has a low early death rate overall, but patients undergoing revision for infection or periprosthetic fracture face a 3 to 4 times higher risk of death within 90 days compared to those revised for wear. The extent of the surgical revision does not affect mortality risk.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Patello-Femoral and Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: A Propensity-Matched Analysis at Two, Five, and 10 Years.
articles.authors: Wang CX, Morriss N, Greif DN, Ghattas YS, Kenney R
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing patello-femoral arthroplasty (PFA) or unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) for isolated knee arthritis
articles.sample_size: 978 patients per group at 2 years, 635 per group at 5 years, 226 per group at 10 years
articles.outcomes: Rates of knee arthroscopy, revision surgery, conversion to total knee arthroplasty, postoperative infection, and implant survivorship at 2, 5, and 10 years
articles.take_home: Both PFA and UKA had similar long-term survival and similar rates of conversion to full knee replacement over 10 years. However, PFA patients needed follow-up arthroscopy procedures more often than UKA patients, which is an important consideration when deciding between these two operations.

articles.title: More Tech-Savvy Than You Think: Digital Proficiency Among Total Joint Arthroplasty Patients.
articles.authors: Lam AD, Parikh N, Valenzuela M, LaGreca M, Hobbs J, Saxena A, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective survey of digital device proficiency
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip or knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of smartphone use and proficiency in navigating menus, typing, sending emails, checking appointments, entering calendar events, and sending pictures by email, compared between patients aged under 65 and 65 years or older
articles.take_home: Older patients having joint replacement surgery are nearly as comfortable with basic smartphone skills like typing and email as younger patients, though they are less confident with more complex tasks like checking appointments or adding calendar events. These findings suggest that simple digital tools could work well for collecting patient feedback after joint replacement surgery.

articles.title: Temporal Trends in Surgical Site Infections After Hip and Knee Arthroplasty in California, 2015 to 2024.
articles.authors: Haji Boloori F, Kubiak A, Meyers M, Nelson B, Perkins M, Ciolacu I, et al.
articles.population: Hospitals in California performing primary hip and knee arthroplasty procedures
articles.outcomes: Surgical site infection rates after total hip arthroplasty and total knee arthroplasty, stratified by hospital volume, policy period, and year
articles.take_home: Surgical site infections after hip and knee replacement remain rare and stable in California, occurring in less than 1% of procedures. Hospital size, public reporting policies, and the COVID-19 pandemic had no significant impact on infection rates.

articles.title: Periarticular Injection Cocktails for Pain Management After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.authors: Ng MK, Mastrokostas LE, Mastrokostas PG, Mont MA
articles.study_type: Systematic review of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative pain, opioid consumption, early functional outcomes, patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: Periarticular injection cocktails reduce pain and opioid use after knee replacement compared to placebo, with similar effectiveness to nerve blocks. Cocktails containing corticosteroids may work better, but no single best formulation has been identified yet.

articles.title: Anterior tibial translation in anterior cruciate ligament-deficient knees is increased regardless of tear location and independently associated with early-to-intermediate injury chronicity.
articles.authors: Hingsamer V, Arras C, Mueller MM, Nash G, DiFelice GS
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament surgery
articles.outcomes: Preoperative anterior tibial translation side-to-side difference measured with a Lachmeter digital arthrometer
articles.take_home: Anterior tibial translation remained increased in all types of ACL tear. Whilst injury timing affected measurements slightly, only the time since injury was independently linked to anterior tibial translation after accounting for other factors, suggesting ACL tear location alone is not a reliable predictor of knee stability.

articles.title: The association between passive anterior tibial subluxation and anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction failure.
articles.authors: Gao YT, Shi WL, Zhong YF, Wen T, Qiu LF, Zhou SP, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients who underwent primary ACL reconstruction between January 2019 and December 2023
articles.sample_size: 262 patients (131 with graft failure matched to 131 controls with intact grafts)
articles.outcomes: Association between passive anterior tibial subluxation (PATS) measured before surgery and ACL graft failure; longitudinal changes in PATS over time
articles.take_home: Patients with greater forward movement of the shin bone before ACL surgery had a higher risk of their graft failing later. Those whose grafts failed showed progressive increases in this forward movement over time, compared to those with successful grafts.

articles.title: Fourfold higher graft failure risk with isolated BPTB versus hamstring ACL reconstruction with ALL in patients under 25 years: A prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: Santamaria F, Carrozzo A, Pioger C, Vieira TD, Sonnery-Cottet V, Fayard JM, et al.
articles.study_type: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Patients under 25 years undergoing ACL reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Primary: graft failure at 5 years. Secondary: KOOS, IKDC, Lysholm and Tegner scores
articles.take_home: Young patients having hamstring ACL reconstruction with additional anterolateral ligament repair had significantly lower graft failure rates (4.8%) compared with bone-patellar tendon-bone reconstruction alone (16.4%), though both groups reported similar satisfaction scores at 5 years.

articles.title: The 2026 ESSKA-ESA formal consensus on partial-thickness posterosuperior rotator cuff tears (Part 2): Treatment strategies, rehabilitation, return to sport and complications.
articles.authors: Kany J, Iban MR, Calvo E, Rosso C, Peach C, Dias CM, et al.
articles.population: Patients with partial-thickness posterosuperior rotator cuff tears
articles.sample_size: 33 questions evaluated by 20 independent shoulder surgeons
articles.outcomes: Treatment strategies, rehabilitation protocols, return to sport timelines, and surgical complications including postoperative stiffness and retear rates
articles.take_home: Non-surgical treatment should be tried first for at least 6 months. If surgery is needed, the choice between different repair techniques should be tailored to each patient based on their activity level, symptoms and tear characteristics, as no single surgical technique works best for everyone.

articles.title: Bicruciate-retaining versus cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty in implant fixation: a 10-year follow-up of a randomized RSA trial.
articles.authors: Kinoshita T, Mortensen KRL, Ingelsrud LH, Muharemovic O, Gromov K, Troelsen A
articles.study_type: Randomised controlled trial with 10-year follow-up using radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Tibial component migration (maximum total point motion), Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score, reoperations and revisions
articles.take_home: After 10 years, both types of knee replacement showed similar implant stability and patient satisfaction. However, the bicruciate-retaining approach had more complications requiring further surgery, suggesting the standard cruciate-retaining knee replacement may be safer for most patients.
